changes: Name normalized to 'Paramānandaprakāśa' (the ācārya title stripped from 'Prakāśācārya' into titles); confidence lowered to medium because it is unclear whether 'Prakāśa' belongs to the personal name
Month read: 'krāṃ ra' is most likely Hindi kvār/kuār, i.e. Āśvina. This fits 'durgāttīja' (Durgā-tṛtīyā, the third day of the autumn Navarātri, Āśvina śukla 3)
Notes expanded on the era and the month

date.as_written: śrīsaṃvat 1851 ke krāṃ ra śuddhi śrīdurgāttīja 3 śanivāra

place.as_written: śrī kāśī svakṣetre śrīmaṇI karṇikā varttate śrīgopālamaṃdirasthāne

notes: The colophon says only 'śrīsaṃvat 1851'. In a Kāśī context with a Hindi-style date ('1851 ke … śuddhi'), 'saṃvat' normally means Vikrama Saṃvat, which gives about 1794 CE. The catalogue's 'ŚS 1851' (= 1929 CE) is not supported by the wording. 'ke krāṃ ra' is probably '[saṃvat 1851] ke kvāra/kuāra', Hindi for Āśvina. That agrees with 'durgāttīja' (Durgā-tṛtīyā, Āśvina śukla 3). The weekday (Saturday) has not been checked. The scribe's name could be read as Paramānanda with the title 'Prakāśācārya', or as the ascetic-style name Paramānandaprakāśa with the title ācārya. The place of copying is the Gopāla temple near Maṇikarṇikā, Kāśī.
